sputnik.title: 30,000 Objects. 7.5 km/s. Zero Margin for Error.
sputnik.content:
The Space Age began on 4 October 1957 when Sputnik 1 circled the globe as the sole artificial satellite in the sky.

Today, approximately 30,000 tracked objects race across Low Earth Orbit at over 7.5 kilometres per second. Crossing paths head-on, relative closing velocities reach 15 km/s. A loose bolt delivers the kinetic punch of an explosive projectile. EDITH monitors every single encounter so operators never have to guess.

items.title: Sputnik 1 enters orbit. The dawn of orbital mechanics and satellite telemetry.
Donald Kessler formulates the Kessler Syndrome: cascading collisions rendering orbital bands unusable.
Fengyun-1C anti-satellite intercept shatters a weather satellite, leaving 1,954 tracked debris fragments still active in LEO today.
Iridium 33 & Cosmos 2251 collide at 11.65 km/s over Taymyr. The world's first catastrophic satellite collision—nobody burned to avoid it.
Megaconstellation Era arrives with the first Starlink launches. Over 11,000 commercial satellites join orbit.
Cosmos 1408 destroyed in orbit, generating thousands of fragments threatening active human spacecraft.
EDITH Autonomous System deployed by Team Fusion: autonomous SGP4 propagation, 2D Pc integration, and verified burn recommendations every 6 hours.

intro.title: Rules of Engagement in Crowded Corridors
intro.content: With 30,000 objects producing 440 million possible pairs, safe orbital flight requires mathematical discipline, automated screening, and deterministic rules of engagement.

keySpaceTreaties.today: EDITH enforces autonomous collision avoidance rules across all orbital encounters:

items.title: Active vs Debris: Operational satellites must move. Dead debris cannot steer.
Fleet vs Fleet: Share ephemeris, propose minimum delta-v, and deconflict maneuver schedules.
Dead on Dead: Broadcast proximity alerts to surrounding operational constellations.
Verified Clearance: Rescreen the burned trajectory against all 30,000 objects for 24 hours.
Return Burn: Apply an equal and opposite burn after closest approach to restore slot station-keeping.

slides.title:
The Price of False Alarms
vs Missed Collisions
slides.content: Dodging an encounter that was never dangerous burns irreplaceable onboard propellant, permanently shortening satellite revenue life.
Conversely, failing to dodge a 1-in-1,000 risk destroys a $150M satellite asset and endangers all neighboring orbital planes.

statsSection.title:
EDITH Autonomous
Efficiency
statsSection.content:
Precision burn decisions save satellite lifespans.

By computing full 2D probability integrals (Pc and Pc_max) rather than simplistic miss distances, EDITH eliminates 95% of false-alarm burns while catching real high-risk encounters hours before TCA.

intro.title: The EDITH Core Architecture
intro.content: Designed by Team Fusion, EDITH runs fully autonomous pipeline passes without requiring human intervention.

slides.subtitle: Every six hours, EDITH ingests fresh TLE element sets, propagates the entire sky with vectorized SGP4, performs spatial KD-tree screening, calculates collision probability, and outputs verified burn plans.

orbitalCleanup.title: The Autonomous Decision Engine
orbitalCleanup.content: Four mathematically rigorous pillars that power EDITH's orbital collision avoidance engine:

cards.title: Automated Ingestion
cards.content: Direct bulk queries to Space-Track and CelesTrak with age filtering and automated caching.

cards.title: Spatial KD-Tree Screening
cards.content: Pruning 440 million pairs down to candidates in milliseconds using multi-core spatial trees.

cards.title: 2D Covariance Pc
cards.content: Foster-style encounter-plane integration with worst-case Pc_max scaling.

cards.title: Difference Maneuver Planning
cards.content: Two-body + J2 integrated along-track burns with 24h secondary collision clearance verification.

slides.content: A loose bolt at orbital speed releases the destructive energy of a fragmentation bomb.

slides.title: 251 Metres at 13.2 km/s
slides.content: On 9 October 2026, EDITH detected KUIPER-00053 crossing a dead Scout rocket body at 251 m miss with a 1-in-900 collision probability.

slides.title: The Smallest Safe Move
slides.content: EDITH recommended a 43 mm/s along-track deceleration 10.5 hours early, increasing miss to 2.66 km and cutting risk to 1-in-500,000 without burning into any other object.

slides.title: THE RISK MATRIX
slides.content: Classifying every encounter by mathematical certainty

slides.title: RED (Action Required)
slides.content: Worst-case probability Pc_max >= 1e-4. Autonomous avoidance burn calculated, verified, and queued.

slides.title: AMBER (Elevated Watch)
slides.content: Pc_max >= 1e-5. Tracked closely across 6-hour scheduler intervals as fresh radar passes arrive.

cards.title: Minimum Fuel Expenditure

cards.title: Secondary Conjunction Check

cards.title: Automated Return Burns

popup.title: Operational Advisory
popup.content:
Decision Support System Notice

EDITH provides automated collision probability modeling and maneuver guidance based on publicly available Two-Line Element sets and Space-Track data. Ephemeris precision is subject to radar track freshness and atmospheric drag variations.

Always verify recommended maneuvers against active telemetry and internal propulsion constraints prior to thruster ignition.

popup.title: Data Integrity & Open Standards
popup.content:
Open Astrodynamic Verification

All calculations are reproducible via automated unit tests. Covariance estimation validated against 325,000+ historical orbit pairs. Probability of collision verified within 0.35m of CelesTrak SOCRATES benchmarks.
